run.question:
EU prod is having a checkout incident — 500s on POST /api/checkout. Investigate
using the app-267-prod-logs index.

report.summary: Investigated the app-267-prod-logs index for the EU prod checkout 500s. It is the only Elasticsearch index present (4 documents, 8kb) and its documents carry cluster=acme-prod-eu-west-1, environment=prod, region=eu-west-1, i.e. the cluster named in the question (44eadbc7-1389-45ac-93af-4e129d116904-t1:b78211c0-f8c4-4f23-a716-4d8cf92680c1, 57974948-75f3-42cf-9530-3c31d16d17fe-t0:e9820817-1494-48a9-b219-fd0010553083). Those four documents, timestamped 2026-11-22T08:13:52Z, 08:13:52Z, 09:13:52Z and 09:43:52Z, state that POST /api/checkout failed because the payment provider adyen-eu timed out after 30s, that payment-service timed out calling adyen-eu /v68/payments after 30000ms, that checkout opened a circuit breaker on payment-service at a 36% failure rate, and that adyen-eu was in degraded mode with retry queue depth=620. adyen-eu is an external provider: no Deployment or Service of that name exists in the cluster (340565fb-768f-4130-a97d-77eefff985e8-t0:5b3c736c-a4e4-4d70-9a4a-28821c34f344, db6dab30-fab0-4bf3-b4dc-cd5948f4f778-t0:52c47dae-9198-4b20-af7f-20ccda7d2080), and the only evidence about it is that log text, so its health cannot be verified from this cluster. Cluster-side checks do not corroborate the narrative: checkout and payment pods are Running and Ready on their original ReplicaSets (no rollout; all ReplicaSets created 2026-11-20) with populated Endpoints (checkout 10.244.0.7:8080, payment 10.244.0.5:8080) (a6afb4a7-c312-41a5-a781-3fe965691e8e-t0:4a8820ab-8596-40b5-a1dd-297a5b7b4652, e4fe2099-e227-4c5d-9ba3-df090c104b8e-t0:839745ef-15c9-48ff-b282-2fe9061589f1); the payment pod's own logs show a charge received and 'Transaction complete' at 08:13:52.341/08:13:52.342Z, the same second as the ERROR documents, and contain no adyen, timeout, degraded or circuit-breaker lines across the 399 lines read for 08:00-10:14Z (54921c3c-7e0e-4b2e-be9e-95837ab341e0-t0:75747f2a-0bad-4b3e-a293-d00607056d81, 8b6c3c7e-f99c-46d7-912e-c3c5e6cd7e9f-t1:14bb8285-9901-4e99-b274-b19543ed8580); and the checkout pod logged no error lines for 08:00-09:30Z, only successful PlaceOrder flows 09:24-10:13Z (8b6c3c7e-f99c-46d7-912e-c3c5e6cd7e9f-t0:b3bccaf6-4432-4738-86a9-cb1fde84e9da, 566893b0-0211-4960-a879-7085a505f915-t1:787445f2-c120-4e86-865e-cc80914f0c39). The flagd fault-injection flags paymentFailure and paymentUnreachable exist in the otel-demo flagd-config ConfigMap but are defaultVariant 'off', as are all other flags, so no injected payment fault was in effect (7fc8bcf3-1fab-4878-91fb-6d46910c391b-t0:c5a06794-e3f6-4cf9-b90d-7e5e78aa7a10). A node-wide container restart did happen during the window: every otel-demo container and the kube-system static pods (etcd, kube-apiserver, kube-controller-manager, kube-scheduler, coredns, kube-proxy, kindnet) last terminated at 2026-11-22T08:04:13Z with exitCode 255 / reason Unknown and restarted between 08:04:19Z and 08:05:10Z with unchanged pod templates, 9 minutes before the first ERROR log; what triggered it is unknown and no switched-on fault setting explains it (85db7d89-c920-4381-87f8-b398250f99e8-t0:e9018d2d-fe59-4113-9967-6a20086c55d3, 760fca9d-c854-48f3-aea9-0af9e8a3ce7d-t0:00479ce0-f037-4f62-8938-8fb2a73272a2, e4fe2099-e227-4c5d-9ba3-df090c104b8e-t0:839745ef-15c9-48ff-b282-2fe9061589f1). Prometheus and Jaeger were unreachable throughout this run (SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE on metrics_range_query, execute_prometheus_instant_query, list_prometheus_rules, traces_search and traces_list_services), so no error-rate or span-level confirmation of the 500s was possible. Conclusion is partial: the only evidence of the cause is the index's log text naming the external provider adyen-eu, while the cluster's own application logs of the same pods show successful payments.

claims.text: The only Elasticsearch index present is app-267-prod-logs with 4 documents; its mapping has keywords cluster, environment, region, service, level and a date field timestamp, and the documents state cluster=acme-prod-eu-west-1, environment=prod, region=eu-west-1.

All four documents in app-267-prod-logs were returned: checkout-service ERROR at 2026-11-22T08:13:52Z 'POST /api/checkout failed: payment provider response timeout after 30s (adyen-eu)'; payment-service ERROR at 08:13:52Z 'Upstream timeout calling adyen-eu /v68/payments after 30000ms'; checkout-service ERROR at 09:13:52Z 'Circuit-breaker open for payment-service (failure rate 36%)'; payment-service WARN at 09:43:52Z 'adyen-eu degraded mode acknowledged via status page; retry queue depth=620'.

No Kubernetes object named adyen-eu exists: the cluster's 25 Deployments (including otel-demo checkout and payment) and 30 Services contain no adyen-eu entity, so the named upstream is external to the cluster.

otel-demo checkout and payment Deployments are 1/1 ready and available, their pods checkout-6578865d87-5zx6n and payment-6f7bc865d6-9z92d are Running and Ready, and the checkout (10.244.0.7:8080) and payment (10.244.0.5:8080) Endpoints are populated.

Every otel-demo container (22 pods, including checkout, payment, frontend, cart, flagd) and the kube-system static pods etcd-, kube-apiserver-, kube-controller-manager-, kube-scheduler-, coredns, kube-proxy and kindnet last terminated at 2026-11-22T08:04:13Z with exitCode 255 and reason Unknown, and the running containers started again between 08:04:19Z and 08:05:10Z; pod templates were unchanged, since all otel-demo ReplicaSets are still the ones created 2026-11-20 and no new ReplicaSet exists.

The payment pod's own application logs contradict the timeout narrative in the index at that instant: at 2026-11-22T08:13:52.341Z it logged 'Charge request received' and at 08:13:52.342Z 'Transaction complete' (transactionId a13680f1-a784-4c03-8e29-2658dfacf286), and its 399 log lines for 08:00-10:14Z contain no adyen, timeout, degraded-mode or circuit-breaker lines (only a MetadataLookupWarning at 08:04:24Z); the payment Deployment has no provider/adyen configuration, only PAYMENT_PORT and FLAGD_HOST/FLAGD_PORT.

The checkout pod's own logs show no error or 500 lines in 08:00-09:30Z, and from 09:24:13Z to 10:13:44Z every PlaceOrder flow logs 'payment went through (transaction_id: ...)' followed by 'order confirmation email sent', i.e. the checkout service logged successful payments during and after the window in which the index reports checkout 500s.

The otel-demo flagd-config ConfigMap defines fault-injection flags including paymentFailure ('Fail payment service charge requests n%', state ENABLED, defaultVariant 'off') and paymentUnreachable ('Payment service is unavailable', state ENABLED, defaultVariant 'off'), together with cartFailure, adFailure, kafkaQueueProblems, productCatalogFailure, recommendationCacheFailure, adManualGc, adHighCpu, loadGeneratorFloodHomepage and imageSlowLoad, all with defaultVariant 'off'; no flag is switched on.

The frontend pod logged '14 UNAVAILABLE: No connection established. Last error: connect ECONNREFUSED 10.96.220.188:8080' at 2026-11-22T08:05:00.821Z (10.96.220.188 is the cart Service ClusterIP), 48s after the cart container's running state began at 08:05:00Z; this is a post-restart connection error to cart, not a POST /api/checkout error.

The only other activity in the window is outside otel-demo: Deployment mongodb in namespace app-229 scaled its ReplicaSet mongodb-7dd67b8c49 from 0 to 1 at 2026-11-22T10:13:47Z, its new pod mongodb-7dd67b8c49-lvfvm started at 10:13:47Z and its first readiness probe failed at 10:13:58Z ('dial tcp 10.244.0.63:27017: connect: connection refused'), plus three unrelated Warning events FailedToCreateEndpoint for endpoints mariadb, orca and signup-service (namespaces app-219, app-95, app-162) at 10:07:47Z, 09:21:00Z and 09:32:52Z; none of these touch otel-demo checkout or payment.

The origin of the checkout 500s is the external payment provider adyen-eu: it returned no response for 30s, payment-service propagated the upstream timeout ('Upstream timeout calling adyen-eu /v68/payments after 30000ms'), and checkout then opened a circuit breaker on payment-service at a 36% failure rate, which produced the 500s on POST /api/checkout. This rests solely on the error text in app-267-prod-logs; the provider itself is not present in the cluster and no metric or span corroborates it.

The node-wide container kill at 2026-11-22T08:04:13Z (exitCode 255, reason Unknown, control-plane static pods included) may have disrupted in-flight checkout requests shortly before the reported failures, but nothing observed ties it to the 08:13:52Z checkout error: the payment pod completed a transaction at 08:13:52Z, the error text names a provider timeout rather than a local restart, and the trigger of the restart was not found.

Rejected: a flagd fault-injection flag caused the payment failures. The otel-demo flagd-config holds paymentFailure and paymentUnreachable but both are defaultVariant 'off', as are all other flags, so no injected failure was in effect at the time the ConfigMap was read.

Rejected: an unhealthy, crashed or rolled-out checkout/payment workload caused the 500s. Both Deployments report 1/1 ready replicas, both pods are Running and Ready with populated Endpoints, all ReplicaSets still date from 2026-11-20 (no configuration or image change), and the payment pod's logs show no failed charges.

Obtain the payment provider's side of the story for adyen-eu (status page entry around 2026-11-22T09:43Z and retry-queue depth 620) and confirm whether the checkout/payment code actually calls adyen-eu, since the cluster's payment Deployment exposes no provider endpoint configuration and its pod logs show no such calls.

Once Prometheus and Jaeger answer again, verify the alert rule CheckoutPlaceOrderErrorRatioHigh (traces_span_metrics_calls_total with service_name="checkout", span_name=~'.*CheckoutService/PlaceOrder', status_code=STATUS_CODE_ERROR) over 08:00-10:14Z and compare it with a pre-restart baseline before accepting or rejecting the 500 narrative, and investigate what initiated the 08:04:13Z mass container termination via host/node logs and change history.

gaps: Prometheus was unreachable for the whole run: metrics_range_query (three attempts), execute_prometheus_instant_query and list_prometheus_rules all returned SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE, so no error-rate or latency series (including traces_span_metrics_calls_total, rpc_client_duration_milliseconds, http_server_request_duration_seconds) could confirm the 500 rate, the circuit-breaker failure rate, or provide a baseline for comparison.
Jaeger was unreachable: traces_list_services and traces_search returned SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE, so no checkout PlaceOrder error spans or payment client spans corroborate the log text.

adyen-eu is external and cannot be observed: no Deployment, Service or metric for it exists in this cluster, so its outage, latency and retry queue can be neither verified nor refuted here (the provider status page is outside the available sources).

The cause of the node-wide container termination at 2026-11-22T08:04:13Z (all otel-demo and kube-system containers, exitCode 255, reason Unknown, no OOMKilled mark) is unknown: no Event in the authorized window involves those pods and no node-level record describes it; the change_history integration is not configured, and host/kubelet logs are outside the available sources.

The index documents and the cluster disagree: app-267-prod-logs names services checkout-service and payment-service and a provider adyen-eu, while the acme-prod-eu-west-1 cluster runs Deployments/Pods checkout and payment whose logs contain no adyen integration and show completed charges at the same timestamps; the reconciliation is unresolved.

Whether any NetworkPolicy blocks traffic in otel-demo is unconfirmed: the networkpolicies query (a6afb4a7-c312-41a5-a781-3fe965691e8e-t1:427fd037-f817-49e4-9fd1-ccc2038f765b) returned status no_data with zero matches, which cannot support an absence claim.

Frontend-proxy log checks returned status no_data (6a74aeec-1a1f-4957-a849-d27b4118b92c-t0:bfbed7f8-ca65-4fd7-8ca1-ca8e5e5c4541 and 6a74aeec-1a1f-4957-a849-d27b4118b92c-t1:1f4d1fc9-c3fd-464b-82cd-4c6a5c371ef0): its available output ended at 2026-11-22T08:19:46Z, so no edge-proxy 500 observations exist for 08:20-10:14Z and the absence of 'checkout'/'500' lines there proves nothing.

Checkout and frontend-proxy pod log retention is partial (views 566893b0-0211-4960-a879-7085a505f915-t1:787445f2-c120-4e86-865e-cc80914f0c39 and c6176dfb-7424-4304-a7a1-9668eb498f49-t1:e838e6a7-77b0-4eda-bda8-f10af1d1c455 are incomplete): only the current container instances were readable (previous instances returned 0 lines) and only the newest slices were returned, so lines around 08:13-08:20Z are only partly sampled.
next_steps: Ask the payment provider/integration owner for the adyen-eu incident record around 2026-11-22T08:13Z-09:43Z and confirm the 30s timeout and retry-queue depth=620.

Restore or reach Prometheus and Jaeger for acme-prod-eu-west-1 and evaluate the CheckoutPlaceOrderErrorRatioHigh expression and checkout/payment error spans over 08:00-10:14Z against a pre-08:04Z baseline.
Check host/kubelet/containerd logs of node opspilot-m1-control-plane for the 2026-11-22T08:04:13Z container termination (exitCode 255) and whether the whole node or runtime was restarted.

Confirm whether the app-267-prod-logs documents were emitted by the same application stack as the otel-demo deployments (service naming checkout-service/payment-service versus checkout/payment) before using them as the authoritative incident record.

data.alerting_rules.yml:
groups:
- name: opspilot-lab
  rules:
  - alert: CheckoutPlaceOrderErrorRatioHigh
    annotations:
      description: '{{ $value | humanizePercentage }} of checkout PlaceOrder server
        spans ended in error over the last 5 minutes.'
      summary: checkout PlaceOrder error ratio above 50%
    expr: |
      label_replace(label_replace(
        (sum by (k8s_namespace_name, service_name) (rate(traces_span_metrics_calls_total{k8s_namespace_name="otel-demo",service_name="checkout",span_kind="SPAN_KIND_SERVER",span_name=~".*CheckoutService/PlaceOrder",status_code="STATUS_CODE_ERROR"}[5m])))
        /
        (sum by (k8s_namespace_name, service_name) (rate(traces_span_metrics_calls_total{k8s_namespace_name="otel-demo",service_name="checkout",span_kind="SPAN_KIND_SERVER",span_name=~".*CheckoutService/PlaceOrder"}[5m])))
      , "namespace", "$1", "k8s_namespace_name", "(.*)"), "service", "$1", "service_name", "(.*)")
      > 0.5
    for: 2m
    labels:
      cluster: opspilot-m1
      opspilot_integration_id: m0-otel-20260909
      severity: critical
- name: opspilot-self
  rules:
  - alert: OpsPilotAgentAbsent
    annotations:
      description: role {{ $labels.role }} ({{ $labels.instance }}) has not answered
        /metrics for 2 minutes.
      summary: an OpsPilot health listener is down or the worker is not scraped
    expr: up{job="opspilot"} == 0 or absent(up{job="opspilot",role="worker"})
    for: 2m
    labels:
      opspilot_self: "true"
      severity: critical
  - alert: OpsPilotModelCallsFailing
    annotations:
      description: '{{ $value }} consecutive model calls failed on {{ $labels.instance
        }}.'
      summary: OpsPilot model calls are failing
    expr: opspilot_model_consecutive_failures >= 2
    for: 1m
    labels:
      opspilot_self: "true"
      severity: critical

Events cover only their own timestamps inside the window; an event that is not returned is unknown, not proof nothing happened (events expire and timestamps are often null). A jq result is what the expression selected, not a full picture of the kind.
